---
title: "Get Started"
subtitle: "Everything you need to go from a raw tracking file to a clean, analysis-ready dataset."
toc: false
---

*animovement* is a collection of R packages that share one data structure and
one workflow. These four guides take you from installing the ecosystem to
reading, understanding, and processing your own movement data. Work through
them in order — each builds on the last.

## [1]{.step-number} [Install animovement](install.qmd)

Install the whole ecosystem (or just the piece you need) from
[r-universe](https://animovement.r-universe.dev), load it, and add the optional
packages some functions rely on.

## [2]{.step-number} [Movement data & the aniframe](movement-data.qmd)

Meet the *aniframe* — the tidy table that every *animovement* package speaks.
Learn how it answers *what* is moving, *when*, and *where*, and how to create
one from scratch.

## [3]{.step-number} [Read your data](read-data.qmd)

Turn an export from *DeepLabCut*, *SLEAP*, *idtracker.ai*, a trackball, or any
of the 18 supported sources into an *aniframe* with a single `read_*()` call —
and grab bundled sample data to follow along.

## [4]{.step-number} [Check & process your tracks](process-data.qmd)

Inspect data quality, drop low-confidence points, fill gaps by interpolation,
and smooth noisy trajectories — all while staying in the same *aniframe*.

::: {.callout-note}
## New to R or the tidyverse?
To get the most out of *animovement*, we recommend getting comfortable with the
basics of R and the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org) first. *animovement*
is tidyverse-friendly: *aniframes* are tibbles, and you can pipe them through
`dplyr`, `tidyr` and friends alongside the `ani*` functions.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Already set up?
If you've installed the ecosystem and know the data model, jump straight to the
end-to-end tutorials in [Learn](../learn/index.qmd), which combine every package
into complete, real-world workflows.
:::
